title: The Gilded Sigil Again
premise: Ada Winterbourne, a debt-bound scribe in the Gilded Sigil guild, has spent years hiding her gift for reading the memories held in ink. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive demanding a census of every gifted soul, Ada's ledgers become both her shield and her danger: they contain proof that the guild itself trades in dragon-fire, the last embers of an ancient war. Torn between duty to the master who owns her debt and love for Corin, a hunter who begins to question his orders, Ada must choose whether to burn the ledgers and expose herself. In the end she releases the last dragon-fire into the world, breaking her debt, saving Corin, and forcing the city to remember what it chose to forget.
about_author: Emrys Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in a rain-soaked port city before turning to fiction. Their novels blend bureaucratic fantasy with quiet, stubborn acts of rebellion.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Ink
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet her in the Sigil's counting-house, transcribing contracts for impossible things while concealing her gift of reading memory from paper. A routine audit nearly exposes her; Master Veyne reminds her that her debt buys her invisibility. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of hiding, and its cost.

chapters.title: A Census of Cinders
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Corin POV. Crown hunters arrive, led by Corin, who interviews guild staff with unsettling gentleness. Ada falsifies entries to protect a gifted child on the rolls, and Corin notices the discrepancy but says nothing. Emotional beat: first spark of trust between enemies, shadowed by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Remember
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Digging for leverage against Veyne, Ada reads a contract written in dragon-fire and experiences the ancient war firsthand—learning the guild helped end it by hoarding the last flame. Veyne catches her and offers a bargain: betray the child, keep her secret. Emotional beat: horror at complicity, grief for a history erased.

chapters.title: The Last Ember Burns Honest
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, alternating POVs. Ada breaks into the vault to free the dragon-fire; Veyne and the hunters converge, and Corin must choose his orders over her. She releases the flame, which floods the city with shared memory of the war. Her debt burns away; Corin stands beside her as the guild falls. Emotional beat: costly, hopeful belonging.
